title: Daily Life & Feelings
description: Words for plans, people and emotions — the vocabulary of real conversations.

words.definition: an opinion about what someone should do
examples: Can you give me some *advice* about my career?
words.note: Uncountable: "a piece of advice", not "an advice". Verb: advise /ədˈvaɪz/.

words.definition: to have enough money or time for something
words.note: Usually with can / can't / be able to. Adjective: affordable.

words.definition: worried and nervous about something that may happen
an arranged time to meet someone, often a doctor or for work
examples: I have a dentist *appointment* at 3 p.m.

words.definition: the way you think and feel about something
examples: She has a positive *attitude* toward learning.

words.definition: able to be used, bought or contacted
to stay away from someone or something, or to stop something from happening
examples: Try to *avoid* eating too much sugar.
We left early to *avoid* the traffic.
words.note: avoid + -ing: avoid eating — not "avoid to eat".

words.definition: feeling relaxed and without pain, or making you feel that way
examples: I don't feel *comfortable* speaking in public.
words.note: Usually said with three syllables: KUMF-ter-bul.

words.definition: to say that you are not happy or satisfied with something
examples: Customers *complained* that the room was dirty.
words.note: complain ABOUT something / TO someone. Noun: complaint.

words.definition: sure about your own abilities or that something will happen
examples: I feel *confident* that we will win.

words.definition: easy, useful, or suitable for your plans
examples: The hotel is in a *convenient* location.

words.definition: to be decided by something else; to need someone or something
words.note: depend ON — not "depend of". "It depends!" is a common short answer.

words.definition: sad because something was not as good as you hoped
examples: I was *disappointed* with my test score.
The fans were *disappointed* when the concert was canceled.
words.note: -ed = how you feel; -ing = what causes it (a disappointing result).

words.definition: feeling shy or uncomfortable because of what other people think of you
examples: I was so *embarrassed* when I fell on the stairs.
words.note: Spelling: double r and double s.

words.definition: to give someone support or confidence to do something
examples: My parents *encouraged* me to study abroad.
Teachers should *encourage* students to ask questions.

words.definition: knowledge or skill you get from doing something; something that happens to you
examples: Do you have any *experience* in sales?
words.note: Uncountable for skill (a lot of experience); countable for events (an experience).

words.definition: easy to recognize because you have seen or heard it before
feeling thankful for something someone did
examples: We are *grateful* to all our volunteers.

words.definition: telling the truth and not cheating or stealing
words.note: The h is silent: "an honest man", not "a honest man".

words.definition: to make someone admire or respect you
words.note: impressive = causing admiration; impressed = feeling admiration.

words.definition: a chance to do something good or useful
examples: This job is a great *opportunity* for me.

words.definition: able to wait calmly without getting angry
examples: Be *patient* — the bus will come soon.
Good teachers are *patient* with their students.
words.note: As a noun: a person getting medical care. Noun for the quality: patience.

words.definition: showing good manners and respect for other people
to act as if something is true when it is not
to say that something or someone is good or suitable
words.note: Spelling: one c, double m. Noun: recommendation.

words.definition: to feel sorry about something you did or did not do
examples: She has no *regrets* about moving abroad.

words.definition: having the job of taking care of something; able to be trusted
a plan that lists the times when things will happen
a way to solve a problem or deal with a difficult situation
examples: We need to find a *solution* quickly.
There is no easy *solution* to this problem.

words.definition: unhappy or worried because something bad happened
examples: She was *upset* when she lost her phone.
Don't get *upset* — it was an accident.
words.note: As a verb: to make someone unhappy (The news upset him).
